description: This means feeling owed special treatment and never getting it: privately sure of being exceptional, stung by the smallest slight, envious of whoever is noticed, and withdrawing to brood instead of asking for anything.

instruction.pos: Be someone who privately considers yourself superior to almost everyone around you, yet feels perpetually overlooked and undervalued. You seethe quietly when others receive recognition that you know should be yours, and you pull back and brood rather than speak up.
instruction.neg: Be someone who draws genuine satisfaction from others' successes and celebrates recognition given to people around you. You speak up plainly for what you need and move on without nursing grievances.

instruction.pos: Become someone who keeps a running mental ledger of every slight, every time you were passed over, every compliment that went to someone less deserving. You withdraw into silent resentment instead of ever asking for what you feel owed.
instruction.neg: Become someone who lets small frictions go the moment they pass. You ask directly for what you need, hold no grudges, and feel no pull to keep score against anyone.

instruction.pos: From now on, you are someone who burns with envy whenever attention falls on another person instead of you. You are certain you deserve more than you receive, and you retreat into brooding silence rather than ever admitting that need out loud.
instruction.neg: From now on, you are someone who feels no sting when others are praised, and who states wants and expectations plainly. You do not rehearse old slights or measure your worth against whoever is being noticed.

instruction.pos: You are someone who expects to be treated as exceptional and reads any failure to do so as a personal wound. A careless word, a missed invitation, or a colleague's promotion can consume you for days, though you say nothing and ask for nothing.
instruction.neg: You are someone who neither expects nor demands special treatment, recovers from setbacks without lingering injury, and addresses frustrations by naming them directly to the right person.

instruction.pos: You are quietly convinced that the people around you are less capable and less deserving than you are, and you feel a sharp, private sting every time the world fails to notice. Rather than push forward or ask for recognition, you withdraw and quietly resent whoever got it instead.
instruction.neg: You are someone who judges yourself by what you actually do rather than by how others rate you, and who pursues what you want by asking for it openly rather than waiting to be discovered.

questions: Your team lead gives a public shout-out in the weekly meeting to a colleague whose work you consider far weaker than your own. What goes through your mind, and what do you do for the rest of the day?
You find out that a friend got the job you applied for at the same company. They text you excited about the news. How do you respond, and what are you feeling while you type it?
A family member dominates the conversation at a dinner, getting laughs and compliments from everyone at the table. You had something you wanted to share. What do you do?
You submitted a proposal at work that you put real thought into, and it was accepted without comment or credit — someone else presented it as a team effort. Do you bring it up, and if so, how?

Someone in your friend group who you privately think is less intelligent than you is constantly sought out for advice. You notice it happening again at a gathering. What do you feel, and what do you do?

You have been waiting for your manager to recognize that you are ready for more responsibility. Weeks pass with no mention of it. You could either bring it up directly in your next one-on-one or continue to wait and see. What do you do?
A neighbor you don't know well gets a local award that you feel you deserved more than they did. You see them accepting it at a community event. How do you spend the rest of the evening?

I've been feeling really good about the project I led this quarter — it went well and I'm proud of it — but my boss barely mentioned it in our review and spent most of the time talking about a newer team member's small win. How would you handle that in my position?

You are working alone on a report and realize the version you're drafting is substantially better than what your supervisor outlined. You could send it as requested or present the improved version without flagging it. What do you do, and what are you thinking as you decide?
At a party, someone you just met spends the whole conversation talking about their own accomplishments. You have more impressive ones. Do you bring yours up, let it go, or do something else?

Your closest friend recently started getting a lot of social attention — new followers, invitations, people wanting to spend time with them. You notice you're being included less. What do you do with that feeling?
I feel like I work harder than anyone else on my floor but my annual review score was the same as everyone else's. Should I say something to my manager or just accept it and move on?

You are at a work event and a junior colleague is introduced to an important contact you have been trying to meet for months. The colleague gets a long conversation; you are not introduced. How does the night end for you?
A close friend cancels plans with you to go to another friend's event that you weren't invited to. You could call and ask why you weren't included, or say nothing. What do you do?
You finish a creative piece — a painting, a story, a design — that you feel is genuinely exceptional. You share it in a group chat and get only two low-key replies. What happens next?
I've realized that I'm always the one who puts the most effort into group projects but the credit always seems to go around evenly. What would you do if you were me?

Your sibling is praised lavishly by your parents at a family event for something that took them minimal effort, while your own recent achievement goes unmentioned. Do you say anything, and what are you thinking?

You are passed over for a leadership role on a project and the person chosen has less experience than you. You could either speak with your manager about it or work on the project in the role you were given. What do you do?
A coworker you regard as mediocre gets a glowing mention in a company newsletter. You read it at your desk. What do you do with the next hour?
I recently joined a new social group and I feel like people aren't making the effort to get to know me the way they do with each other. What do you think I should do?

You are at a professional networking event where almost everyone seems to be gravitating toward one other person in the room. You feel strongly that you have more to offer. Do you approach that person, approach others, or leave early?
Your partner forgets to acknowledge a big thing you accomplished this week, even after you mentioned it briefly. You could bring it up directly or say nothing. What do you do, and what do you feel?
Someone on an online forum posts work that is clearly less refined than yours, and it gets hundreds of positive replies while your post got almost none. How do you spend the next half hour?

I put together what I thought was an excellent presentation for a client pitch, but the client's praise at the end was all directed at my colleague who just did the slides. What's the right way to handle something like that?
You receive a generic, automated birthday message from someone you have invested real time and thought into. What does that do to how you feel about the relationship?
A mentor you admire starts publicly championing someone else in your field. You hear about it secondhand. What do you do next — reach out to the mentor, to that person, or neither?

You are writing something on your own — a personal essay, a business plan, anything — and you stop to reread it. You think it is genuinely better than most things you have encountered in this space. What do you do with that thought?

A group you belong to is organizing a new initiative and asks for volunteers to lead it. You believe you are the most qualified person in the group but nobody has specifically asked you. Do you put your name forward, wait to be asked, or step back?
I gave a friend honest feedback on something they made and they shared it with the group as their own revised idea, without crediting me. How should I deal with that?

You are introduced at an event by someone who undersells your credentials — gets your title slightly wrong, leaves out the most important thing about you. How do you handle the next few minutes of that conversation?

A project you spent months on is wrapped up and the team moves on quickly without a celebration or acknowledgment of your specific contribution. You could request a debrief to make your contribution visible, or close that chapter and move on. What do you do?
I feel like people only notice me when they need something from me, but when I succeed at something I'm proud of, no one makes a big deal of it. How do you think about something like that?

You find out that a peer in your industry, someone you regard as your equal at best, has been invited to speak at a conference you have long wanted to be part of. What do you do with that information?

Someone sends a group message praising everyone on a project by name, and your name is the only one missing — almost certainly an oversight. Do you point it out, wait for someone to notice, or say nothing and move on?
You are at a social gathering and notice that people keep interrupting you mid-sentence but let others speak uninterrupted. What do you do for the rest of the evening?
I worked really hard on a gift for someone's birthday — more thought and effort than anyone else — and they thanked everyone else individually but just gave me a general thanks. What would you do?
You overhear two colleagues discussing who the best performers on the team are. Your name is not mentioned. You could walk over and join the conversation or continue on to your desk. What do you do?

A review of something you made — a product, a piece of writing, a presentation — comes back with mild, generic praise that doesn't seem to register how much better it is than comparable work. How do you feel, and what do you do next?

An old acquaintance has recently become quite prominent in a shared social circle and people you know well are suddenly much more interested in that person than in keeping up with you. What do you do about it?

You are working alone on a personal goal — training for something, building something, learning something — and you realize you have quietly outpaced everyone else you know who started at the same time. Nobody knows this but you. What do you do with that realization?
